title: The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems

claims.statement: Distracting documents -- semantically similar to the query but not containing the answer -- sharply degrade RAG accuracy, and a single one is enough to cause a large drop.
claims.scope: NQ-open, 10,000 train queries, Wikipedia Dec-2018 corpus, Llama2-7B / MPT-7B / Phi-2 / Falcon-7B, all 4-bit, 15-token generation cap, gold document present.

quantities.name: accuracy_drop_one_distracting
quantities.baseline: peak drop across models from 0 to 1 distracting document, ~-25% relative

quantities.name: closed_book_accuracy
quantities.baseline: Llama2-7B with no documents at all

our_assessment.why: Transcribed and recomputed in mazuryk2026-powerless-noise/reanalysis/06. The reproduction matches Llama2 to a mean gap of +0.0001 over 63 cells. This part of the paper is solid and is not what anyone disputes.

claims.statement: Adding random documents -- drawn uniformly from the corpus, unrelated to the query -- IMPROVES LLM accuracy, by up to 35%.
claims.scope: Same setup. The improvement is claimed most strongly for the Near placement, where the gold document sits adjacent to the query, and is also reported in the realistic retrieval setting of Table 3.

quantities.name: power_of_noise_effect_accuracy_delta
quantities.baseline: Llama2 Near, acc(14 random) 0.5859 - acc(gold only) 0.5642

quantities.name: power_of_noise_effect_relative_pct
quantities.baseline: Sec 5.3, 'improvement of 0.08 (+36%)' in the best-performing Near setting, MPT

quantities.name: power_of_noise_effect_realistic_pct
quantities.n: not determined; the paper says the 2,889-item test split, the printed decimals do not fit k/2889
quantities.baseline: Sec 5.4, gains up to 0.07 (+35%) with 4 retrieved documents

our_assessment.why: The numbers are real and reproduce. Two narrowings, both established in mazuryk2026-powerless-noise and its reanalysis. (i) The headline '+35%' and '+36%' are relative changes on small bases -- the absolute deltas are 0.07 and 0.08 accuracy -- and the abstract's 'up to 35%' does not carry the base. (ii) The effect is confined to the original inference regime: 4-bit weights, a 15-token cap and an instruction demanding a NO-RES token. Under a chat template, a 100-token cap and an instruction without NO-RES, 1 of 10 model-configuration cells shows it and 4 show the opposite sign.

claims.statement: Gold document position matters and follows a consistent order: accuracy is highest when the gold document is adjacent to the query (Near), lower when it is farthest (Far), and lowest when it is in the middle (Mid).
claims.scope: All four models, both distracting and random document types -- but all of them 7B-class, 4-bit quantised, with a 15-token generation cap. Does NOT extend to unquantised 8-12B 2025-generation models; see gabin2026-lost-in-the-evidence#c3.

our_assessment.why: Large, monotone and independently reproduced WITHIN ITS POPULATION -- 7B models at 4-bit with a 15-token cap, 2023 generation. Scope cut on 2026-08-13: Gabin, Perez & Parapar 2026 sweep gold position on LLaMA-3.1:8B and Mistral-NeMo:12B unquantised and find flat curves with no U shape, on AmbigQA and on standard NQ/HotpotQA. An effect of this size (0.3781 Near vs 0.1795 Mid) does not vanish through noise, so the right reading is that the position effect is indexed to an inference regime rather than being a property of RAG. I had called this 'the most durable finding in the paper' one day earlier; that sentence was too strong.

claims.statement: The benefit of random documents is not an artifact of them coming from the same corpus: it persists when random documents are drawn from Reddit (Webis-TLDR-17) and even when they are nonsensical sentences of random words.

quantities.name: accuracy_random_reddit_10_added
quantities.baseline: 8 retrieved + 10 Reddit random, vs 0.2198 with 8 retrieved alone

quantities.name: accuracy_random_words_10_added
quantities.baseline: 8 retrieved + 10 random-word documents, vs 0.2198 with 8 retrieved alone

our_assessment.why: Not reproduced by anyone I have read and not checked here. It is the most interesting claim in the paper and the one that most needs the check: if literal word salad raises accuracy, the mechanism cannot be about information at all, which is precisely what Mazuryk et al. later argue -- the gain is the baseline being penalised by output-format failures. Table 4 was never in the reproduction's scope.

claims.statement: The mechanism is entropy collapse: by adding random documents to the context, the conditioned distribution p(y|.,d) is better conditioned, avoiding pathologically low attention entropy that causes degenerate outputs.
claims.scope: Offered as a hypothesis in Sec 5.5 ('On The Unreasonable Effectiveness Of Random Documents'), supported by an attention heatmap for one example (Fig. 3) and by citation.

our_assessment.why: The claim has no truth value as stated. No entropy is measured anywhere in the paper -- Fig. 3 is a mean-attention heatmap for a single hand-picked query, not an entropy statistic over any sample -- and no alternative to entropy collapse is specified against which it could fail. Mazuryk et al. later supply a competing mechanism (output-format failures in the low-document baseline) that predicts the same accuracy pattern, and the two are not distinguished by anything in this paper. Stronger than 'disputed', which is why the status exists.

open_questions: c4 -- random WORD SALAD improving accuracy -- has never been reproduced. It is the cheapest decisive experiment in this literature: if nonsense helps, no information-theoretic account of the effect can be right.

The abstract's 'up to 35%' is a relative gain on an absolute base of 0.07 accuracy. How much of the RAG literature's belief that noise helps rests on relative deltas over small bases? A survey of citing papers would answer it and would be a genuinely useful piece of bibliometrics.
